  ### Overview
  
  If main's dev server isn't answering, `berthd shots compare` makes exactly one fallback attempt. It uses the current worktree's own **`turn-start`** baseline, a set of PNGs saved earlier by `berthd shots baseline`. Two conditions must hold: you passed no `--base`, and `<shotsDir>/<loc>/<wt>/baselines/turn-start/baseline.json` exists. When the fallback happens it prints a `note:` line, and the result is filed under a different visual-diff artifact. If either condition fails, the compare refuses with a message telling you to start main's server or take a baseline.
  
  Several things you might expect don't exist. Nothing starts main's server for you. There is no git ref or merge-base baseline, no reuse of a previous run's "before" images, and no fallback to the `accepted` baseline or any other named one. There are no `--url` or `--against` flags (`shotsArgs` rejects unknown flags). The only base selector is `--base main|turn-start|accepted|NAME`. Baselines have no staleness check at all.
  
  ### Key Concepts
  
  - **`ShotsRequest.Base` / `--base`**: an empty value means "main, with a fallback allowed". An explicit `main` means "main, no fallback". Any other value is a baseline name matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,39}$` (`internal/box/shotsstore.go:251`).

result:
If main's dev server isn't answering, `berthd shots compare` makes exactly one fallback: your worktree's own `turn-start` baseline. That only happens when two things are true:

- You didn't pass `--base` at all.
- `<shots>/<loc>/<wt>/baselines/turn-start/baseline.json` exists.

When it falls back, it prints a `note:` line and files the result under a different visual-diff artifact. Otherwise it refuses with "nothing to compare with", telling you to start main's server or take a baseline. I checked this in `internal/box/shots.go:314-352`.

Several things you might expect don't exist:
- Nothing starts main's server for you.
- There's no git ref or merge-base baseline.
- A previous run's "before" images are never reused.
- It never falls back to `accepted`.
- There are no `--url` or `--against` flags. The only selector is `--base main|turn-start|accepted|NAME`.

## How it decides

All of it happens in `planShots` (`internal/box/shots.go:253`), before any browser starts.

1. **Your worktree must be up first.** The command finds which port belongs to your worktree and checks that something answers on it. If nothing does, it errors (`shots.go:304-306`). This applies to every `--base`, including `turn-start`. `shots baseline` (which sets `Save`) stops here and never looks at main.
2. **No `--base` is treated as `main`, but a fallback is still allowed.** The code records `explicit := req.Base != ""` before replacing an empty value with `"main"`.
3. **Main counts as unusable in three cases** (`shots.go:321-335`):
   - The location has no main checkout.
   - You are running from the main checkout.
   - Nothing answers on main's dev port (`answers(ms.dev)` fails).
4. **If main is live**, it shoots main through `http://<loc>.<box>.localhost:1377` and stores the result under the artifact key `visualdiff:main`.
5. **If main is unusable**, it checks whether `turn-start/baseline.json` exists. If you passed `--base` explicitly or the file is missing, it errors. Otherwise it sets `base = "turn-start"` and the notice "…; compared with the turn-start baseline instead".
6. **Saved baselines** are any non-main base, whether you asked for it or got it by fallback. The name is validated, `readBaseline` loads it, and each "before" image is read from disk. A page missing from the baseline is reported as "NEW: not in the baseline".

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[shots compare] --> B{worktree dev port answers?}
  B -- no --> E1[error: start your dev server]
  B -- yes --> C{--base given?}
  C -- "no / main" --> D{main exists, isn't you, main's port answers?}
  D -- yes --> M[shoot main live; artifact visualdiff:main]
  D -- no --> F{--base main given explicitly?}
  F -- yes --> E2[error: start main or take a baseline]
  F -- no --> G{turn-start/baseline.json exists?}
  G -- no --> E2
  G -- yes --> T[base = turn-start + note; artifact visualdiff:turn-start]
  C -- "turn-start / accepted / NAME" --> H{baseline readable?}
  H -- no --> E3[error: no NAME baseline yet]
  H -- yes --> S[load saved PNGs as 'before']
  T --> S
```

**How "main's port" is found:**
- "Main" is the first entry of `git worktree list` (`locations.go:474`), whatever branch it has checked out.
- Its dev port is the lowest listening port tied to main's checkout (`browserScopeWith`, `browserproxy.go:215`). A port counts if it falls in main's 10-port block from `PortAlloc`, or if the process listening on it was started from inside main's directory.
- `answers()` is a 1-second TCP dial to `127.0.0.1` (`shots.go:221`).

## Gotchas

- **No staleness check.** A baseline stores `Commit`, `Taken` and the Chromium version. Only a Chromium mismatch adds a note; nothing compares the commit or the age. The `--as` login isn't recorded either, so a logged-out `turn-start` compared with `--as` diffs a logged-out page against a logged-in one, with no warning.
- **The fallback answers a different question.** `turn-start` is your own worktree's pages at an earlier moment, not main's pages. Anything you changed before taking it won't show. Nothing creates it automatically: it exists only if someone ran `berthd shots baseline` or set up the opt-in `agent.started` hook (`docs/guides/visual-diffs.mdx:153-163`).
- **A fallback lands in a separate artifact.** The artifact key uses the base actually chosen, so if main goes down between runs you get a new `visualdiff:turn-start` instead of a new version of the main comparison.
- **The TCP-only check can misjudge main.** These follow from the code; none has been tested:
  - A main server that returns 500s still counts as up, so you get ERROR rows instead of a fallback.
  - Any other listener in main's port block or directory can make main look up.
  - A main server started outside main's directory and outside its block isn't tied to main, so main looks down.
  - So does a server bound only to `::1`.
- **Running from main** with no `--base` quietly uses `turn-start`, with the note "this is the main checkout".
- **Misleading error text.**
  - With an explicit `--base main` and an existing `turn-start`, the message still tells you to take a baseline.
  - A `baseline.json` that exists but is corrupt gets past the existence check, then fails with "has no "turn-start" baseline yet".
- **Docs vs. code:**
  - The skill, `visual-diffs.mdx:92` and the changelog only mention the "main isn't running" fallback. The other two triggers (no main checkout, running from main) aren't documented.
  - `visual-diffs.mdx:191-192` says log-in isn't supported, which contradicts line 100 of the same page and the `--as` code.

## Where things live

- `internal/box/shots.go`: `planShots` makes every decision; also `answers` and `ShotsCompare`.
- `internal/box/shotsstore.go`: baseline layout, save and load.
- `internal/boxcmd/shotscmd.go`: CLI flags; `shots baseline` defaults to `turn-start`.
- `internal/box/browserproxy.go` and `services.go`: which ports count as a checkout's.
- Baselines on disk: `$BERTH_HOME/box/shots/<loc>/<wt>/baselines/<name>/`, keyed by location, worktree and baseline name, not by branch or SHA.
- Test: `TestShotsBaseFallsBackToTurnStart` (`shots_test.go:334`).
